messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 Pager - GPU pool 'inference-prod' queue growth detected. queue_length > 95% of capacity for 10m, autoscale failing. Alert: gpu_pool_utilization_high. Pager: @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: Ack, I'm on it. seeing 5xx spikes and long queue times in the gateway. Can someone grab HPA + metrics-adapter logs?

infra-eng: grabbing nodes + hpa state now. `kubectl get hpa -n prod | grep inference` shows desired 120 -> current 40 (max 40). HPA at max replicas.

ml-platform: Confirmed queue backlog on the inference-queue. Many requests are piling onto GPU worker pods and being throttled. Metrics adapter latency looks high.

chris: throwing prometheus query: `sum(rate(inference_queue_depth[1m])) by (pool)` -> big spike for inference-prod. Also seeing `kube_hpa_status_current_replicas` stuck at 40.

kevin: digging metrics-adapter logs: 
```
I0407 11:02:12 adapter.go:234] scrape latency=18.7s target=prometheus:9090
E0407 11:02:25 adapter.go:501] error converting metrics: series parse error
```
This looks like adapter is dropping scrape responses or timing out.

maria: metrics-server also reporting `connection refused` intermittently to the adapter. Could be network flapping between control-plane and prometheus.

sre-oncall: Immediate mitigation: 1) flip routing fallback to CPU-backed smaller models for non-SLA traffic, 2) provision emergency burst GPUs (request infra to create ephemeral pool), 3) restart metrics-adapter pod to clear stale state. I'll run these.

infra-eng: Starting scale-up request to cloud: provisioning 8xA10 burst nodes. Noted billing impact. ETA ~ 4 min.

ml-platform: Command to flip routing rule (run by eng-runner):
```
redwood-cli routing override set --pool inference-prod --fallback cpu-small --match non_sla
```
I've pushed the change, rolling out now. Expect reduced GPU pressure for low-priority traffic in ~30s.

sre-oncall: Restarting metrics-adapter: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter`

support-bot: Incoming customer reports: multiple customers seeing increased latency and 5xx. Top impacted: acme-inc (heavy batching), dev-analytics (real-time inference). Logging CS cases.

chris: After routing flip we see queue depth drop ~40% in 2m. Good. But high-priority traffic still queues.

kevin: metrics-adapter restart completed, logs look cleaner now. Prometheus scrape latency back to normal for a few targets. HPA metrics now updating.

infra-eng: Cloud nodes provisioned and joined cluster, pods are scheduling onto new GPUs. `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu` shows +8.

ml-platform: HPA now able to scale beyond previous limit because cluster autoscaler recognized new nodes. HPA target moving to 90, current 40 -> scaling.

sre-oncall: Handing off to @maria for monitoring while I create postmortem stub. Maria, please gather prometheus scrape history and metrics-adapter traces for the timeline.

maria: Ack, taking over. I've pulled metrics from 10:52-11:12 UTC and saved to /shared/incidents/2723456789/prometheus_dump.json. Noted a 6m window where adapter returned 500s to kube-metrics.

sre-oncall: Customer impact summary for pager: ~22 minutes of elevated latencies for some customers, ~8 customers with >=1% errors. No data loss, only degraded inference latency and 5xx.

support-bot: Notified affected customers with templated message; escalation flag set for account managers.

chris: Post-fix checks: `kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-deploy -o jsonpath='{.status.currentReplicas} {.status.desiredReplicas}'` -> shows 88  -> 120 (scaling up). CPU fallback removed for SLA routes.

maria: Leaving monitoring on for 1h, will collect additional logs. Filing followup tasks: 1) investigate root cause of adapter parse errors, 2) add extra headroom on HPA max for inference-prod, 3) add alert to detect metrics-adapter scrape error rate earlier.

sre-oncall: Closing page for now — system stabilized and queues back to normal. Will convert to incident ticket and assign actions to infra/plat. Thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> Converted to ticket RED-INC-2026-142. Timeline and logs uploaded.
